HARNESS. release_count_harness.py imports the producer from this tree and calls build_snapshot over one VersionedInputs per firm: once as the code stands, then once with apply_cash_rule replaced by an identity function (restored in a finally). A mover is a SECURITY node whose asset_class differs by node_id (no unmatched node and no duplicate node_id for any firm). The layer of each mover is the producer's classify_security class_source re-run on its display symbol, description and security id; the re-run asset_class equals the built node's for every mover (rerun_asset_class_mismatch 0, all three firms). Movers on another layer: 0.

GATE. gate_before is evaluate_publish_gate on the with-rule candidate with the pre-repair marks rule, written in the harness: every landed directory entry counts, a missing termination indicator counts UNKNOWN, all UNKNOWN and the directory non-empty. gate_after uses the producer's directory_marks_no_closures and closed_account_ids. The served side is read with HoldingsPublication.begin() and served_publication() (read calls only); the served side is live, not pinned.

PINNING. RUN A: each firm at as_of 2026-10-12 (the pin is an input; the order's source date). RUN B: the identical arguments, with VersionedInputs._refs pre-seeded from RUN A's receipts for that firm (a private attribute of the producer's reader; the seeding is the one addition to the arguments). The producer's reader then reads each object at RUN A's version and raises if its bytes differ; RUN B read zero objects outside RUN A's set for every firm. RUN A and RUN B agree exactly on movers, canonical tickers, gate outcomes, conditions, listed lost accounts and the receipts digest for all three firms.

DIGEST. receipts_digest is the sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII) of VersionedInputs.receipts() for RUN A. No object key, version id or account identifier is recorded in this file.
